ORAL JUDGMENT :
1. Heard. Admit.
Heard finally with the consent of learned counsel appearing for the parties.

2. The present application is preferred by the applicants for quashing of First Informant Report in connection with Crime No.228/2018 registered under Sections 363, 376 and 366 r/w Section 34 of the IPC and consequent proceeding arising out of the same bearing charge sheet No.69/2024.
3.
A crime is registered on the basis of report lodged by the non-applicant No.2 alleging that she was aged about 23 years at the time of incident.
The applicant No.1 is her neighbour and they were on the visiting terms of each other's house.

They were also studying in the same school and therefore,
there was acquaintance with each other.
Since 2009, there was love affair between her and applicant No.1 but the applicant No.1 has performed marriage with another girl in the year 2012.

On enquiry by her that why he has performed marriage with another girl, he disclosed that he wants to marry with her only and on the promise of marriage, there was physical relationship between her and applicant No.1.

It is further alleged that her marriage was 3 20-J-APL-1106-2019.doc settled by her father and was scheduled on 23/04/2018, but the present applicant has kidnapped her on 04/04/2018 and in the said kidnapping, other applicants have assisted him.
Thereafter, he took her at his relatives place and confined her and also subjected her for the forceful sexual assault.
On the basis of said report, police have registered a crime against the present applicants.
4. After registration of crime, the Investigating Officer has investigated the matter.
The victim was referred for the medical examination, her medical certificate was also collected.
The samples collected are forwarded to Chemical Analyzer and the relevant statements were recorded and after completion of investigation, charge sheet came to be filed against the present applicants.

5. Heard learned counsel for the applicants who submitted that as far as the assistance by the other applicants in kidnapping is concerned, which is not substantiated by any material only because they are the relatives of the applicant No.1, they implicated in the alleged offence.
She submitted that no specific role is attributed to them as far as kidnapping by them is concerned.
She submitted that applicant Nos.2 to 5 were only present when the applicant No.1 and the victim went together.
Therefore, no offence is made out against the applicant Nos. 2 to 5.
She submitted that the recitals of the FIR and consequent statement shows that out of love affair, the physical relationship was developed between applicant No.1 and non-applicant No.2.
As the marriage was not performed between them, the FIR came to be lodged against the present applicant No.1.

Thus, even accepting the allegation as it is at its face value, no offence is made out against present applicants and therefore, application deserves to be allowed.
6.

Per contra, learned APP and learned counsel for the complainant submitted that considering the statement of the victim that initially, there was love affair but applicant No.1 has kidnapped her on the promise of marriage with the help of other applicants and after his marriage, he has subjected her for the forceful sexual assault is sufficient to attract the offence punishable under Section 376 of the IPC, her consent is obtained under the misconception of fact and therefore, application deserves Anup Rajendra Jadhao And 4 Others vs State Of Mah., Thr. 7. After hearing both the sides and on perusal of entire investigation papers, it reveals that there was acquaintance between the applicant No.1 and non-applicant No.2.

The said 5 20-J-APL-1106-2019.doc acquaintance resulted into the love affair and out of the love affair, there was physical relationship developed between the present applicant No.1 and non-applicant No.2.

From the recitals of the FIR and statements of the witnesses, it reveals that thereafter, the applicant No.1 could not perform marriage with the victim and his marriage was solemnized with another lady.
This fact was known to non-applicant No.2.
Despite she knows the fact, they were meeting each other and physical relationship was continued between them.
Thus, the relationship was from 2009 to 2018 till lodging of the FIR.
As far as kidnapping is concerned, the allegation which is not sufficient to attract the offence punishable either under Section 363 or 366 of the IPC.

8. "Consent is an act of reason accompanied with deliberation, the mind weighing, as in a balance,
the good and evil on each side."

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Uday Vrs. State of Karnataka,
reported in 2003 (4) SCC 46 wherein, it is held that "there does not necessarily have to be complete willingness to constitute consent.
A woman's consent to intercourse may be hesitant, reluctant or grudging, but if she consciously permits it there is consent".

In para No.11 and 12, it is held as under :-
11.

Some of the decisions referred to in Words and Phrases, Permanent Edition, Vol.
8A at p. 205 have held "that adult female's 6 20-J-APL-1106-2019.doc understanding of nature and consequences of sexual act must be intelligent understanding to constitute 'consent".
Consent within penal law, defining rape, requires exercise of intelligence based on knowledge of its significance and moral quality and there must be a choice between resistance and assent.

Legal consent, which will be held sufficient in a prosecution for rape, assumes a capacity to the person consenting to understand and appreciate the nature of the act committed, its immoral character,
and the probable or natural consequences which may attend it".
12.
"The courts in India have by and large adopted these tests to discover whether the consent was voluntary or whether it was vitiated so as not to be legal consent."

9. In a celebrated judgment of Promod Suryabhan Pawar Vrs. State of Maharashtra and another,
reported in (2019) 9 SCC 608 after exhaustively dealing with the case laws related to the subject, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "there is distinction between mere breach of a promise and not fulfilling a false promise.

entities.text: Promod Suryabhan Pawar Vrs. State of Maharashtra and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the Court must examine whether there was made, at an early stage a false promise of marriage by the accused and whether the consent involved was given after wholly understanding the nature and consequences of sexual indulgence.

There may be a case where the prosecutrix agrees to have sexual intercourse on account of her love and passion for the accused,
and not solely on account of misrepresentation made to her by the accused, or where an accused on account of circumstances which he could not have foreseen, or which were beyond his control, was unable to marry her, despite having every intention to do so.

Such cases must be treated differently."

sentences.text: In the instant case, the victim who herself was 23 years old lady developed the love relationship with the present applicant.
The applicant No.1 has performed marriage.
The fact of his marriage was known to her.
Undisputedly, she continued her relationship with him.
After his marriage also, the relationship was continued from 2009 to 2018.

If the entire conduct during the course of such relationship with the accused is closely seen, it seems that out of love for the present applicant No.1,
she continued her relationship which was physical in nature.
As far as consent is concerned, it is now well settled that the consent under the misconception of fact cannot be for years together.

Here,
in the present case, the relationship was continued for at least 10 years between the present applicant and non-applicant No.2.
11.
In view of that, said consent cannot be under the misconception of fact.

Under Section 90 of the IPC, a consent given under misconception of fact is no consent in the eyes of law but the misconception of fact has to be in proximity to the occurrence and cannot be spread over a period of 10 years, it hardly needs any elaboration that the consent of the non-applicant was conscious and informed choice made by her after she knows the fact that the marriage is performed by the applicant No.1.
In 8 20-J-APL-1106-2019.doc view of that, no prima facie case is made out against the present applicants and therefore, the application deserves to be allowed.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass following order :-
ORDER i] The application is allowed.

ii] The FIR in connection with Crime No.228/2018 registered under Sections 363,
376 and 366 r/w Section 34 of the IPC and consequent proceeding arising out of the same bearing charge sheet No.69/2024 is hereby quashed and set aside against the present applicants.
12. The application is disposed of.
